observations: Main-route crates are few (33) and sit where a robot pattern or beam makes collecting them a timing decision.
Hidden Nitros punish overshoot directly behind a staggered stack.
The only green ! is at the end of the death route, which forces the perfect order and a deathless reverse run.
Both life boxes are bonus outlines filled from the far end of the bonus, so collecting them requires a reverse trip over Nitros.
A crate can be both tool and reward: striped steps must survive until the return.

cameraSections.notes: a grated catwalk runs into the screen from the start pipe (D2 1), then turns into left-to-right strips (F2 p077R, p078L strip A).
left-to-right strips C, B and D (F2 p078R, p078L, p078R). C1 and C2 sit where the catwalk turns a corner.
a red/white checker catwalk runs into the screen after C2 (D2 21), then left to right (F2 p079L top, p079R top, p079L bottom).
left to right (F2 p079R bottom, p080L top and bottom); a ramp up to the goal.
one machine room crossed out and back (D2 28–32).
blue-tinted machine corridors (D2 45–48), then normal lighting to the green ! (D2 49–55).

jumpSequences.rhythm: wait for full extension, jump; repeat

F2 POINT6 order: left arrow first, then the gap above the right arrow.
jumpSequences.evidence: F2 p078L POINT6; D2 p069 shot 7

jumpSequences.why: Each hop meets a robot; the arm state chooses the next move.

jumpSequences.evidence: F2 p079L POINT16; D2 p070 shots 33–34

D2 30: jump from the top of this piston to the far right; bounce once from the boxes to the piston on the right, but don't break them yet.
A bounce chain cannot stop in mid-air.

jumpSequences.rhythm: wait for the arms to start closing, then bounce, bounce, long jump

geometryObservations: There are three robots, each with one correct answer, and the geometry is built for that answer. YTYTs (slide only) meet you on flat catwalks long enough to slide. ISGNs (answer chosen by arm state) hover at landings and over voids. Shield researchers stand on tiny pads where a push is death.

The piston has three jobs. It is a ceiling crusher you pass while it is up, a floor lift you ride and leave at full extension, and an enemy partner (it rises with the ISGN's arms in POINT18 and stands behind a researcher in POINT20). The level walks through: single (O-S1-a) → row of four as a wave (O-S1-c) → slow pair you shelter under (O-S2-b) → in-phase pair (O-S2-g) → synchronised with an enemy (O-S4-a) → behind a pusher (O-S4-b) → sequenced in the death route (O-D-a).

Slide is the master verb. It kills YTYTs, passes pipes (a gap only a slide fits), goes under pistons and over plate rows as a slide-jump, and escapes beams. The start strip's Aku tip warns you to think about footing width and the distance to traps when sliding, and POINT3 shows why: a long slide on a short pad ends under a piston.

Catwalks are short and segmented. Gaps are 1–3 u almost everywhere (the piston caps at ≈3–4 u are the exception), and the danger is vertical (pistons, nozzles) or comes from behind (beams), not jump length.
Hot pillars build pens. Two pillars ≈4–5 u apart with a robot patrolling between them make a reusable fenced-enemy module: wait outside, jump in while the robot is far away, kill it (POINT11; D2 22).

Plates turn stopping into the hazard. Each plate fires a beam from behind, so every plate means "don't stop here". The ? on a pedestal next to a plate (S3-b) tempts exactly that stop, and the four-plate row compresses the lesson into one slide-jump (G-S3-e).

Enemies placed before obstacles teach combined timing. A walker behind a pipe, a walker under a piston and an ISGN beside an obstacle each have one move that clears both (POINT9, POINT10, D2 15). This "one input, two problems" design recurs in every strip.

Rest lives at corners and after gauntlets. C1 and C2 sit where the catwalk turns; C3 comes immediately after the plate run. The short researcher pads in S4 are deliberately the opposite: no rest, nowhere to retreat.

Geometry creates a level-wide enemy-conservation puzzle. The turret ledge can be climbed on the way back only by bouncing on one ISGN (G-S3-a). Killing it on the way out breaks the box-gem run, so an enemy's survival becomes part of the route (D2 25; p100R).

The death route turns robots into platforms. ISGN bounce chains cross voids (G-D-b, G-D-c), and the timing window is the arms closing ("stomp just before"), so the enemy pattern is the platform cycle.

One new element per strip, then combinations. The start strip introduces YTYTs and pistons, strip A ISGNs and floor pistons, strip C the ISGN arm drill, strip B pipes with walkers under pistons, and strip D hot pillars. S3 adds beams and plates, S4 shield researchers, and the goal strip combines piston, plate and walker.

Crates as tools in the bonus. The striped steps are the only safe footing over the Nitros and must survive until the return (D2 30). The bonus also ends with the level's signature move, a long jump from a piston at full extension (G-B-b).
geometryTransfer: Crusher wave: four `crusher`s ≈1.5 crates (≈1.7 m) apart with `phase` stepping ≈0.2 s each, so a 9 m/s run that starts as the first one lifts passes all four (POINT4). For skaters at 12 m/s, widen the spacing to ≈2 crates (≈2.3 m) to keep the same timing.

Floor-piston stepping stones: use `mover` pads on `axis: "y"` (1.5-crate caps, ≈1.7 m) rising to the next catwalk height, ≈3 crates (≈3.5 m) apart. At full extension the hop is an easy full jump (≈5.6 m reach); at the bottom of the cycle the next cap is out of reach. That teaches "jump at full extension".

Fenced enemy pen: two one-crate posts ≈4–5 crates (≈4.6–5.8 m) apart, with a `grunt` (or a `charger` for the test version) patrolling between them on `range` ≈2 crates. The player waits outside and hops in when it is far. On the board, a full-charge ollie (≈1.7 m) clears a one-crate post (1.15 m), so the pen also works on a skate line.

Slide-only gaps: a low bar across a catwalk at ≈0.8 m clearance forces a slide. Put a stompable `grunt` approaching from the far side so the slide also kills it (POINT10). Keep such bars off skate lines unless they are built as grindable rails.

Plate pursuit with existing kinds: there is no plate-triggered turret. Approximate it with a `sentry` aimed down a catwalk from behind a crate pedestal, so stopping to break the crate gets you shot, and give the player a slide or spin answer.

Enemy as the step back: put a stompable enemy below a ledge 5+ crates high (≥5.8 m, above the double-jump reach of ≈4.6 m). Only a stomp bounce (≈3 m) plus a double jump reaches it, so a player who kills the enemy early loses the way back. Use it only for an optional return route, as Crash does.
